rules: Every meaningful user request must have a stable requirement ID.
Original user intent must not be silently deleted when implementation details change.
IMPLEMENTED requires repository evidence; VALIDATED requires explicit test evidence.
A green compile does not imply PIE, device, performance or visual acceptance.
Open requirements remain in the ledger across developer/chat handoffs.

requirements.title: Permanent repository-based project memory
requirements.origin: User requirement recovered and reaffirmed after lost/deleted chat
requirements.intent: Record requests, decisions, completed work, incomplete work, validation state and next actions so the project survives forgotten details, deleted chats and programmer changes.
missing_work: Requirement ledger itself must become mandatory CI input
Every future meaningful user request must be added/updated
Need periodic reconciliation between ledger, checkpoints and current state
acceptance_criteria: New programmer can identify all open high-priority requirements without reading chat
Each implemented requirement links to code/data/checkpoint evidence
Unfinished user requests remain visible
CI rejects missing core memory artifacts
requirements.notes: This entry intentionally distinguishes existing recovery docs from the stronger all-user-requests ledger.

requirements.title: Large-project source organization and handoff map
requirements.intent: Keep source ownership and target structure explicit so the runtime module can scale and another developer can continue safely.
implementation_refs: 43 runtime module source/build files are mapped to domains and target Public/Private paths
missing_work: Physical Public/Private domain migration is not yet performed
acceptance_criteria: All runtime source files represented exactly once in architecture manifest
Physical migration passes static validation and real UE4.27.2 build
No gameplay redesign mixed into migration
requirements.notes: Current layout remains flat but guarded.

requirements.title: World must feel continuously alive during traversal
requirements.origin: User requirement reaffirmed after lost chat
requirements.intent: Wherever the player moves, encounter believable life, activity, ambience, discoveries and environmental motion instead of empty travel space.
implementation_refs: ambient NPC routines and player awareness
instanced foliage and ambient audio foundations
acceptance_criteria: Ordinary traversal repeatedly reveals believable activity or environmental storytelling
Activity responds to region/story state
Target laptop performance remains acceptable
Each chapter records living-world acceptance separately
requirements.notes: Full requirement is not satisfied by current social pauses alone.

requirements.title: Rich cinematic geography and biome identity
requirements.origin: User requirement for mountains valleys water beauty and film-like travel
requirements.intent: Worlds need strong geography: hills, valleys, rivers, forests, mountains, landmarks, occlusion, vistas and chapter-specific atmosphere.
missing_work: Most non-Shire regions remain prototype geometry
acceptance_criteria: Each chapter has recognizable physical identity
Traversal uses elevation, occlusion and reveal rather than flat arenas
Production visuals pass device/performance and visual acceptance
requirements.notes: Biome plan exists but final production quality is incomplete.

requirements.title: NPCs need believable routines awareness and social life
requirements.intent: NPCs should feel like inhabitants with purpose rather than static quest markers.
missing_work: persistent named-NPC continuity beyond current story state
acceptance_criteria: NPC behavior varies by role/location/story state
Named NPC continuity survives save/load where required
Distant simulation remains cheap
Behavior passes target-device performance
requirements.notes: Existing ambient behavior is a foundation, not the final intelligence system.

requirements.title: NPC-to-NPC contextual conversations
requirements.origin: User explicitly requested NPCs converse with each other
requirements.intent: NPCs should greet, gossip, work-talk and react to local/story events with short context-aware conversations.
evidence: Current source only proves social pauses; no complete NPC-to-NPC dialogue exchange is claimed
acceptance_criteria: Two eligible NPCs can exchange context-appropriate lines
Conversation does not repeat excessively
Story knowledge boundaries are respected
Main quest dialogue always has priority
Performance is bounded
requirements.notes: Do not confuse existing face-to-face social pause with implemented conversation.

requirements.title: Bounded NPC dialogue creativity and knowledge limits
requirements.origin: User requested a limited degree of NPC creativity and dialogue intelligence
requirements.intent: NPC dialogue may vary and react intelligently, but only inside authored identity, knowledge, canon and story boundaries.
implementation_refs: authored dialogue intents and story-aware dialogue foundations
acceptance_criteria: NPC never reveals knowledge it should not know
No canon-changing invention
No verbatim screenplay reproduction
Variation remains coherent with speaker/location/story state
System works without requiring an always-on expensive model on target laptop
requirements.notes: Preferred design is bounded intelligence with deterministic fallback, not unrestricted free generation.

requirements.title: Persistent named-NPC memory and relationships
requirements.origin: Recovered from user's desire for persistent intelligent inhabitants
requirements.intent: Important NPCs should remember selected interactions/events and maintain bounded relationship context when it improves continuity.
evidence: Current route/story persistence exists, but no general named-NPC memory/relationship system is claimed
implementation_refs: existing save architecture can provide integration foundation
acceptance_criteria: Important memories persist through save/load
Memory cannot alter mandatory story outcomes
Save footprint remains controlled
Ambient crowds use cheaper aggregate state

requirements.title: Reliable save load and route continuity
requirements.intent: Player progress, location, story and parallel-route state must survive save/load and Frodo/Gandalf switching.
implementation_refs: F5 save verified historically; route snapshots implemented
missing_work: F9 round-trip verification on current build
acceptance_criteria: F9 restores expected transform/story state
F8 preserves Frodo state through Gandalf route
automatic checkpoints cannot skip required story results
requirements.notes: This remains a blocker before major new gameplay features.

requirements.title: Large living world must remain playable on target laptop
requirements.intent: All world/NPC intelligence and visual ambition must respect the low-spec target rather than becoming an unbounded simulation.
implementation_refs: one major generated region at a time
missing_work: focused target-device traversal/performance observation for current production Shire
acceptance_criteria: 30 FPS floor target at 720p Low/Medium without severe memory pressure or unplayable hitching
requirements.notes: Performance evidence must accompany living-world expansion.

requirements.title: Film trilogy is the authoritative story spine
requirements.origin: User reaffirmed that the project is an experiential adaptation of the films, not a newly invented story
requirements.intent: Use the established film chronology, major characters, locations, conflicts and required outcomes as the primary narrative blueprint. The game may enrich gaps but must not replace the film story with a different one.
implementation_refs: P1C01-P1C08 Part I route follows the film continuity
Gandalf/Isengard parallel route fills a film-canon event outside Frodo's viewpoint
missing_work: Make film-to-game coverage machine-readable for all Part I runtime chapters
Part II and Part III remain roadmap/design rather than production-complete
acceptance_criteria: Every major implemented story beat maps to film continuity or an explicitly tagged compatible gap-fill
No game-authored side content changes required film outcomes
Chapter handoffs preserve the known chronology
Part I coverage gaps are visible in repository data rather than hidden in chat
requirements.notes: Books/lore may enrich the world only when they do not silently overwrite film continuity.

requirements.title: Player should live the film as a playable adventure
requirements.origin: User explicitly described the goal as feeling personally inside the film and living the adventure
requirements.intent: Translate major film moments into player experience: traversal, exploration, interaction, stealth, combat, social scenes or interactive cinematic presentation instead of reducing the project to passive cutscenes or a generic quest list.
implementation_refs: Bree through Amon Hen runtime greybox skeleton
missing_work: Chapter-by-chapter film-experience coverage and treatment audit
Many major scenes are still prototype or compressed
Final cinematic/gameplay blends, character performances and production environments
acceptance_criteria: Major film anchors are experienced through appropriate gameplay or interactive presentation
Player agency exists where it does not contradict required story outcomes
Important emotional/story moments are not skipped merely to connect quests
Each chapter records which film anchors are covered, partial or missing
requirements.notes: The goal is experiential fidelity, not verbatim screenplay reproduction.

requirements.title: Exploration freedom between fixed film story anchors
requirements.origin: Derived directly from the user's request to adventure and explore while remaining inside the film story
requirements.intent: Let the player wander, discover life, talk to characters, use side routes and encounter optional details between mandatory film anchors, while the major chronology and outcomes remain stable.
implementation_refs: Shire exploration loops and side stories
missing_work: Define exploration envelopes around each chapter's fixed anchors
Add more optional discoveries and living-world activity outside Shire
Verify exploration cannot skip or invalidate mandatory story results
acceptance_criteria: Player can meaningfully explore between mandatory story beats
Optional content does not overwrite film chronology
Returning to the main route remains readable
No free-roam shortcut can silently bypass a required story outcome
requirements.notes: Freedom belongs between anchors, not instead of anchors.

requirements.title: Machine-readable film-to-game scene coverage
requirements.origin: Inferred from the user's requirement that the known film story should be systematically applied rather than forgotten
requirements.intent: Maintain a machine-readable Part I coverage map that records the important film anchors for each runtime chapter, intended game treatment and current coverage state.
implementation_refs: FilmExperiencePlan created for P1C01-P1C08 plus GandalfParallel
missing_work: Keep coverage states synchronized as chapter implementation changes
Expand anchors only when useful without turning the file into a copied screenplay
Add Part II/III coverage only when those production scopes open
acceptance_criteria: Every P1C01-P1C08 runtime chapter has film anchors in the plan
Every anchor declares treatment and coverage state
Missing/partial film anchors remain visible to future developers
Guardian rejects loss of required chapter/parallel-route coverage
requirements.notes: Coverage uses high-level scene intent and event labels, never screenplay text.
